subject: Archival granularity & roll‑forward playbook — backup purge windows / DPA impact
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: DataTransferOps <dto@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Archival granularity: backup purge windows & DPA impact

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we sign the final SOW we need clarity on how Redwood handles backups and log retention relative to our DPA commitments. A few specific asks:

- Primary data deletion: when a customer requests deletion (or under DSR), how long before the same data is removed from backups and snapshot tiers?
- Backup purge windows: do you purge backups in a single sweep or do you use staggered windows (e.g., per region or per subprocessor)?
- Subprocessor involvement: we see third‑party backup vendors listed in the preliminary subprocessor inventory. Which subprocessors have access to decrypted data vs. metadata only?
- Log retention exceptions: Acme requires an option to retain audit logs for 18 months in cases of billing dispute or regulatory inquiry. Is that possible as an exception?

We'd appreciate an outline of the deletion workflow, timelines (RTO/RPO not necessary here, just purge timings), and any DPA addendum language you recommend. I've attached our internal retention policy for reference.

Laura Chen
Director, Privacy & Data Governance
Acme Health

Attachment: acme-retention-guidance.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Archival granularity: backup purge windows & DPA impact

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the clear list. Looping in Karthik (infra) and Marissa (customer success / contracts) so we can give an end‑to‑end answer. Quick summary while we compile the details:

- Short answer: we support a staged deletion flow (immediate deletion from active stores; backups purged on a configurable, staggered cadence; and legal‑hold exceptions available per agreement).
- We'll send a proposed staggered purge schedule (by retention class) and a draft DPA addendum that captures an 18‑month audit‑log exception mechanism.

Action items:
1) Karthik — can you attach the current subprocessor inventory and a high‑level matrix of which subprocessors handle encrypted vs decrypted copies?
2) Marissa — can you prepare DPA addendum language and confirm whether an exception for 18 months is doable from a billing / commercial perspective?
3) I will put together a one‑page playbook for Acme that shows the timeline from deletion request -> active store wipe -> backup purge -> final compliance confirmation.

We aim to get a first draft back by EOD Friday 10/30 PST. If that works, I'll follow up with links.

Thanks —
Hannah
Senior Manager, Customer Privacy (Redwood Inference)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Archival granularity: backup purge windows & DPA impact

Hi all —

Following up with the infra details Laura asked for. Attached: subprocessor_inventory_20261028.csv and a draft "staggered_purge_schedule.xlsx" (high level). Key points:

- Active store deletion: when we receive a verified DSR/erase call, primary records are removed within 24 hours from the active index and flagged for immediate GC.
- Backup strategy: we use a layered backup approach across two vendors: S3 Glacier (region‑native snapshots; vendor: AWS) and BackSafe (cross‑region archival snapshots). Backups are encrypted at rest; keys are in our KMS.
- Decrypted access: only our internal infra services have transient access to decrypted tokens for restore operations; BackSafe receives encrypted snapshots and metadata only — BackSafe cannot decrypt without Redwood‑managed keys.
- Purge cadence options: we support configuring purge windows per retention class — common patterns we offer: 30/90/180/365 days after deletion from active store. Purges are executed in rolling batches by region to avoid capacity spikes.
- Staggered purge behavior: rolling batches are scheduled over a 14–21 day window per region for large accounts; for smaller accounts we can do a 48–72 hour window.

Notes on exceptions:
- Legal hold / audit exceptions: we can place a hold that prevents purge for a defined window (configurable) and emit an audit trail entry. For Acme's request (18 months), we can support that as an exception via DPA addendum, but ledger entries and retention accounting will be enabled and billed accordingly (see Marissa).
- Cross‑border transfer: if any backups move between regions, the transfer is done encrypted in transit and subject to subprocessors list updates — we'll flag any cross‑region movements to Acme.

I've attached the two files; comments inline in the schedule sheet (column G) about burst vs. rolling purge modes.

—Karthik
Director, Infra & Reliability

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20261028.csv, staggered_purge_schedule.xlsx

Subject: Re: Archival granularity: backup purge windows & DPA impact

Hi Laura —

Thank you for the specificity; this helps. From a legal / DPA perspective:

- DPA addendum: we've drafted an addendum that: (1) enumerates eligible retention classes, (2) allows for mutually agreed exceptions for audit/forecasting/billing disputes, and (3) requires written request + PO for exceptions that incur additional storage/processing fees.
- 18‑month audit log exception: acceptable as an addendum item. The addendum will require: start/end dates for the exception, explicit scope (audit logs only, not primary PII), and a monthly surcharge to cover extended retention and eDiscovery readiness.
- Subprocessor disclosures: we'll update the subprocessor appendix to mark which vendors have access to decrypted data and which hold encrypted-only snapshots. We will provide a signed notice when a material subprocessor change occurs.

Next steps:
1) Marissa — please confirm commercial terms for the 18‑month exception and draft the PO language.
2) Hannah / Karthik — please approve the redlines in the attached dpa-addendum-draft.docx; we'll then route for signature.

I can loop our contracts team into the DocuSign flow once we have the accepted redline.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations (Redwood Inference)

Attachment: dpa-addendum-draft.docx

Hi Laura —

Thanks everyone. Confirming commercial and operational position so we can finalize the addendum and SOP:

- 18‑month audit log exception: Approved as an addendum item. Surcharge: US$0.0015 per log‑entry/day (estimate) — we'll provide an exact forecast after we ingest your log volume sample. Exception will require a signed PO and will be billed monthly.
- Purge schedule: Proposed default for Acme: primary deletion immediate; backups purged at 30/180/365 days based on classification tiers (we mapped your tiers in the attached staggered_purge_schedule.xlsx). Rolling purge across regions over 14 days for the 365 tier.
- Subprocessors: we will provide weekly updated CSV for the initial 30 days after contract signature, then monthly thereafter. Per Kim, any material change triggers notification.

- Final DPA addendum redline (Kim)
- One‑page deletion->purge playbook for Acme with timeline visuals (Hannah)
- Finalized pricing estimate for the audit‑log exception based on Acme sample (Marissa)
- DocuSign envelope prepped for signature (Contracts)
